family.description: The structure of tRNA(Ile)-lysidine synthetase consists of an N-terminal dinucleotide-binding fold domain (NTD), and a C-terminal globular domain (CTD). The structure of the NTD closely resembles that of a P-loop "N-type" ATP pyrophosphatase [[cite:PUB00034489]]. These proteins belong to the PP-loop superfamily [[cite:PUB00014303]].
family.name: PP-loop domain

history.description: Saved review 20261011T094436Z-pf01171-tils-modification-and-aminoacylation assesses three graphs and eight direct observed effects in defined biochemical preparations. Exact P52097 and cited Z50870 mapping, stop-omitting primer design, whole-protein scope, intact-mass localization limits, unrepurified preparations, separate S100 and purified B. subtilis IleRS contexts, normalization and contamination limits remain explicit. Native projection validation passed during review; this is same-agent partial scientific assessment, not independent endorsement or complete family characterization. Exact clone scars, carryover controls, uncertainty, original intermediate studies and later ortholog evidence remain follow-up work. Status remains IN_PROGRESS.

causal_graphs.context: 75 ul, 50 mM TAPS pH 8.5, 3 mM MgCl2, 0.5 mM TCEP, 0.1 mg/ml BSA, 20 uM transcript, 100 uM ATP and 500 nM TilS; 37 C for 4 h. Use 0.1 mM lysine in B or 20 mM ethanolamine in H. Preparations are frozen without further workup; product gels, intact-RNA MS and residual-substrate radiolysine assays are distinct readouts.

evidence.explanation: Table 4 B versus A, visually inspected Figure 2 B lanes and preparative Methods; the mass discrepancy is within the paper's reported error.
Exact reference and source-accession mapping; other TilS domains remain part of the experimental protein.

edges.mechanism: Reaction B shifts the tRNA gel band and gives an intact mass consistent with the expected lysine-modified product. This supports net modification, not independent proof of its exact bond geometry or site from mass alone.
edges.subject: tils-atp-transcript-lysine

evidence.explanation: Table 4 H versus A and Figure 2 H lane, distinct from the contaminated K/L reactions.

edges.mechanism: Reaction H yields a shifted tRNA species and an intact mass consistent with ethanolamine addition. The 20 mM alternative substrate condition is not evidence that this product normally occurs in cells or that its catalytic efficiency equals lysine's.
edges.subject: tils-atp-transcript-ethanolamine

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P52097/TILS_ECOLI, tilS/mesJ/yaeN/b0188, 432 aa, sequence version 1. UniProt, InterPro and cited Z50870.1/CAA90751.1 match exactly; PF01171 spans 10-197. Published primers match the coding start and terminal WQKTLS, excluding the native stop for a reported C-terminal His6 fusion. Complete vector scar and experimental clone are not independently reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole TilS also contains C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains. Neither isolated PP-loop sufficiency nor a directly tracked adenylation/nucleophilic-attack sequence follows from these data. Raw spectra, exact modification-site localization, replicate counts and uncertainty are unverified here. N-alpha-methyllysine and ornithine samples gave lysine-like products attributed to contamination, not confirmed alternative incorporation.

causal_graphs.context: Dilute frozen modification mixtures to 100 nM tRNA in 30 ul of 50 mM HEPES pH 7.3, 10 mM Mg(OAc)2, 100 mM KCl, 0.5 mM TCEP, 0.1 mg/ml BSA, 100 uM ATP, 100 nM tritiated isoleucine or methionine, and 40 ug/ml S100 protein. Two hours at room temperature, followed by acidic SPA capture.

evidence.explanation: Table 5 A/B E. coli IleRS column and synthetase-assay Methods; normalized to B, not tRNAMet.

edges.mechanism: The B preparation supports a higher isoleucine-incorporation signal than A, reported as 100 versus 2 on the E. coli IleRS column's own scale. It is a preparation-level biochemical effect, not a direct observation of anticodon hydrogen bonding.
edges.subject: use-lysine-modified-preparation

evidence.explanation: Table 5 A/B E. coli MetRS column, its distinct normalization footnote and matched assay protocol.

edges.mechanism: The B preparation gives less detected methionine incorporation than A, reported as 0 versus 23 on the MetRS column's tRNAMet-normalized scale. This is a bounded assay loss, not a universal impossibility of methionylation.
edges.subject: use-lysine-modified-preparation

evidence.explanation: Table 5 A/H E. coli IleRS column, linked to the mass-supported Table 4 H preparation.

edges.mechanism: The H preparation increases isoleucine incorporation relative to A, reported as 123 versus 2. The graph does not interpret 123 versus B's 100 as a statistically established improvement over the natural modifier.
edges.subject: use-ethanolamine-modified-preparation

evidence.explanation: Table 5 A/H E. coli MetRS column, not purified MetRS or an in-vivo decoding experiment.

edges.mechanism: The H preparation lowers detected methionine incorporation relative to A, reported as 0 versus 23 on the MetRS-specific scale. Carryover and detection limits remain explicit.
edges.subject: use-ethanolamine-modified-preparation

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The modifying enzyme is intact P52097-associated TilS, PF01171 10-197 plus its C-terminal domains. S100 reporter enzymes and transcript are separate components; the graph does not assign their catalysis to PF01171.
causal_graphs.limitations: Preparations were not repurified, so residual amine, ATP and TilS may carry over. The causal comparison is between reaction preparations, not purified RNAs proven to differ at only one atom. Table 5 columns use different normalization references; values are not absolute cross-enzyme rates. No replicate/error estimates or universal zero-activity threshold are supplied, and no in-vivo AUA decoding is measured here.

causal_graphs.context: Reaction B or H preparations diluted to 100 nM tRNA, 0.1 nM recombinant IleRS, 100 nM tritiated isoleucine and 100 uM ATP in the 30-ul HEPES pH 7.3 synthetase assay with 10 mM Mg(OAc)2. Two hours at room temperature; acidic SPA capture. Compare each preparation with no-amine A.

evidence.explanation: Table 5 A/B B. subtilis column and recombinant IleRS/assay Methods; 100 versus 0 on that column's scale.

edges.mechanism: The lysine-modified preparation supports greater isoleucine incorporation than the no-amine preparation with purified B. subtilis IleRS. This does not transfer the exact E. coli extract rate or its enzyme composition.
edges.subject: lysine-preparation-with-bsubtilis-ilers

evidence.explanation: Table 5 A/H B. subtilis column and Table 4 H identity, with mixed-species and carryover qualifications.

edges.mechanism: The ethanolamine-modified preparation also supports increased incorporation relative to A, reported as 99 versus 0. Similarity to B is not treated as proof of identical kinetics or physiological substitution of ethanolamine for lysine.
edges.subject: ethanolamine-preparation-with-bsubtilis-ilers

causal_graphs.family_mapping: P52097 TilS supplies PF01171 at 10-197 and produces the tested preparations. The partner accession Q45477 identifies B. subtilis 168 IleRS, not a PP-loop-family enzyme. Its current sequence version 3 is later than the 2009 experiment; complete historical FLAG construct identity is not independently reconstructed.
causal_graphs.limitations: This mixed-species result is not a native cellular pathway or evidence for B. subtilis TilS activity. The B/H preparations are unrepurified and may retain reaction components. The reported 100/99 values have no supplied uncertainty establishing equivalence, and the zero control is bounded by assay detection. No codon recognition or translation rate is measured.

The structure of the NTD closely resembles that of a P-loop "N-type" ATP pyrophosphatase [[cite:PUB00034489]]. These proteins belong to the PP-loop superfamily [[cite:PUB00014303]].

evidence.explanation: Tables 4/5 and Figure 2 support the adopted effects; contamination, isotope dilution, preparation carryover and normalization limits are retained.
Later ortholog-specific recognition findings identify additional work; methods, exact member mappings and figures were not fully reviewed.

discussions.notes: Resolve experimental clone scars, carryover controls and error estimates; inspect the original adenylated-intermediate and recognition studies before adding those microsteps. Curate remaining true alternative substrates separately from contaminated ornithine/N-alpha-methyllysine samples. Extend the 2025 ortholog study after member mapping and Methods/figure assessment. Do not infer cellular decoding, drug efficacy or family-wide chemistry from these preparations. Partial same-agent scientific review; remain IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Extend TilS evidence with exact constructs, modification-site chemistry and ortholog-specific substrate recognition.
discussions.rationale: Eight observed cell-free assay effects cover two product preparations and separate aminoacylation systems. They do not establish a fully observed atomic mechanism, purified-RNA-only causality or the activities of every PP-loop protein.
